hexapod.headline: Strong prototype; sharpen the experiment and flight operations.
hexapod.strengths: Faculty praised inclusion of the whole team, the requirements and hypotheses, the working prototype, and the clear safety treatment with a linked ESDP draft. The work schedule was checked positively. [p. 1: Org Chart, Baseline design, Safety, Work schedule, Prototype]

priorities.title: Clarify the application and measurement problem.
priorities.faculty_feedback: The overview was rushed and unclear. Reviewers requested a specific CDR application, justification of the relevant vibration frequencies, response versus frequency, and a method for measuring error. [p. 1: Overview; p. 2: General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Prepare a focused problem statement and a test matrix connecting vibration inputs, frequency range, measured response, and error metrics.

priorities.title: Make flight operations explicit.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers asked about the vibration source, operator number and locations, payload location, motion-sickness risk across gravity phases, and whether there are two controllers for 0G and 1.8G. Attachment of the payload was an assumption to clarify. [p. 1: ConOps; p. 2: General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Provide a labeled operations diagram and phase-by-phase procedure that resolves each question; confirm how the payload is mounted.

priorities.title: Improve design communication.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers requested explanatory text on CAD and highlighted the budget slide's CAD/text diagram as a useful example. [p. 1: Baseline design]
priorities.suggested_action: Annotate the main CAD view so a reader can identify components and their functions without narration.

hexapod.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated

phytogarden.headline: Convert the background research into a defined, testable flight design.
phytogarden.strengths: Faculty recognized the images and inspiration, extensive background research, and geometrical prototypes. [p. 1: Overview, Prototype, General notes]

priorities.title: Restore missing review elements.
priorities.faculty_feedback: The consolidated form identifies the team introduction, safety analysis/mitigation, and work schedule as missing. A scanned review also emphasizes containment during the brief experiment. [PDR_reviews.pdf p. 6: Safety] [p. 1: Org Chart, Safety, Work schedule]
priorities.suggested_action: Add team roles, a hazard-and-mitigation assessment, and a dated schedule leading to the next review and flight readiness.

priorities.title: Define the microgravity experiment.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers could not identify the required 0G tests, specific ConOps, test apparatus, or final design clearly. They requested progress on microgravity justification and measurements, and instructed the team to separate air and water channels. [p. 1: Overview, Baseline design, ConOps, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Show the selected design and separate channels; justify the geometry and capillary behavior, and specify what occurs during the flight window, the apparatus, and measurements. [Additional basis: PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 6-7]

priorities.title: Make the essential story presentable.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Too many slides prevented coverage. Reviewers asked for an 8-10 slide summary, supporting material in an appendix, citations, and an explanation of TPMS. [p. 1: Overview, Baseline design, ConOps, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Build and rehearse a concise deck covering every required rubric element, with references and expanded acronyms.

phytogarden.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated

active-textiles.headline: Specify the material choices and demonstrate a contained experimental process.
active-textiles.strengths: Faculty noted good initial mass mock-ups and a promising start to the system. The open questions were considered appropriate for PDR leading toward CDR. [p. 1: Prototype, General notes]

priorities.title: Resolve containment and experimental operations.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Although Safety is checked positively, the narrative requires a closed system and testing of that closed system. The cleaning phase, equipment and people locations, and assurance that dust reaches the sample were unclear. [p. 1: Safety, ConOps]
priorities.suggested_action: Provide a containment test plan and operations diagram showing dust delivery, cleaning, and personnel positions. Explain how performance can be observed inside the closed system and evaluate simplification. [Additional basis: PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 2-3]

priorities.title: Justify materials and simulant choices.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers could not determine which fabrics and methods were selected; baseline details were missing. They questioned the chosen dust simulant and whether it represents the fractal nature of lunar dust. [p. 1: Overview, Baseline design, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Identify selected fabrics, cleaning methods, and simulant; explain the comparison to lunar dust and limits on the conclusions the test can support.

priorities.title: Add execution and communication details.
priorities.faculty_feedback: The consolidated rubric requests a schedule, but the individual evidence is mixed: Fincke circles that row (p. 1), while Jeff checks both columns (p. 23). Verify whether the schedule was absent, overlooked, or insufficiently clear. Reviewers also cautioned about unexplained acronyms. [PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 1, 23] [p. 1: Work schedule, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Add a milestone schedule and expand acronyms at first use.

active-textiles.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated

lumbar-puncture.headline: Preserve the clear presentation while strengthening the data and operational rationale.
lumbar-puncture.strengths: Faculty praised the introduction, references, baseline description, GUI, and operational presentation. They noted effective answers to questions and excellent time management. Every row in the consolidated rubric is checked in both columns; individual comments still request refinements. [p. 1: rubric and General notes]

priorities.title: Justify the amount and timing of data collection.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers asked whether the plan includes only one lumbar puncture in flight and whether one ground and one inflight procedure yield sufficient data. They also asked how long the procedure takes. [p. 1: Baseline design, ConOps]
priorities.suggested_action: Specify planned repetitions, timing, measurements, and what conclusions those observations can support. Explain feasibility within the available flight windows.

priorities.title: Refine operator setup and contingencies.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers recommended examining relevant ISS operations videos and clarifying operator and other personnel positions. They raised tether complications, broken needles, spare parts, glove considerations, and item management in the glove box. Sticky-side-up duct tape was a suggestion. [p. 1: ConOps, Safety, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Prepare an operator layout and contingency procedure addressing these points; evaluate the suggested item-management approach rather than treating it as an approved safety solution.

priorities.title: Tighten the scientific framing.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers requested qualifying the problem statement to refer to some astronauts. General notes mention measuring operator stress before and after measurements. [p. 1: Overview, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Revise the problem statement and clarify pre/post operator stress measurement. Rebalance presentation detail: Fincke says perhaps too much time was spent on ligament design, despite praising overall time management. [PDR_reviews.pdf p. 14: Prototype, General notes]

lumbar-puncture.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated

catena.headline: Retain the strong technical work and resolve the flight-transition plan.
catena.strengths: Faculty praised the CAD and prototype. The consolidated rubric praises the R&D simulation environment, while Fincke questions an R&D object-replacement element; whether these refer to the same feature is unresolved. [PDR_reviews.pdf p. 16: General notes] The schedule was present in the deck, although presentation time ran out. [p. 1: Baseline design, Prototype, Work schedule, General notes]

priorities.title: Address pullout and containment.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers repeatedly asked how the system handles 0-2G pullout and 2G during flight. Containment advice differs: Fincke suggests an enclosed volume, explicitly not a net; another sheet conditionally suggests a net if recovery can be assured. Operator positions and roles also need clarification. [PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 16, 18] [p. 1: ConOps, Safety, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Show the gravity-phase operating plan, operator roles, and proposed containment approach. Present the competing containment options for faculty resolution and document how the design addresses pullout; do not treat a net as agreed guidance.

priorities.title: Choose the application and explain novelty.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Many applications were listed; reviewers requested a final choice for CDR and asked why the particular folding sequences were selected and what is new. [p. 1: Overview, Baseline design]
priorities.suggested_action: State one selected application, the folding-sequence rationale, why the design is round, and the specific novel contribution. Clarify the final idea that a reviewer found unclear. [PDR_reviews.pdf p. 18]

priorities.title: Improve presentation access and timing.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers requested the team introduction up front, relocation of unreadable detailed electronics to backup material, and better timing and clarity. [p. 1: Org Chart, Baseline design, General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Lead with the team, use readable system-level figures, and rehearse a timed deck that reaches the schedule and safety material.

catena.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated

vitabee.headline: Condense the presentation and make the flight test achievable.
vitabee.strengths: Faculty called the project interesting and the prototype good. The baseline included a block diagram, CAD, and extensive requirements. [p. 1: Baseline design, Prototype; p. 2: General notes]

priorities.title: Cover safety and justify the test configuration.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Safety coverage was insufficiently clear: Jeff says it was not dealt with, while another sheet says it was covered briefly and requests more information. [PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 19, 21] Reviewers asked whether the cylinder will have wax, requested references, and wanted a clear explanation of the need for microgravity assessment. [p. 1: Safety, Overview]
priorities.suggested_action: Add a hazard-and-mitigation assessment, identify the cylinder configuration, and distinguish the proposed microgravity test from prior flight work noted by a reviewer. [PDR_reviews.pdf p. 21]

priorities.title: Simplify and check operational feasibility.
priorities.faculty_feedback: The ConOps was difficult to read and spread across many pages. Reviewers considered three tries per parabola very hard and suggested considering one. [p. 1: ConOps]
priorities.suggested_action: Prepare a one-page ConOps diagram with detailed procedures in the ESDP. Check trial timing and evaluate a one-try-per-parabola plan; the review does not establish that this plan has been validated.

priorities.title: Prioritize essential presentation content.
priorities.faculty_feedback: Reviewers requested everyone's photo, less time on the overview, requirements moved mostly to appendix/ESDP, and an 8-10 slide main deck. The presentation ran out of time. Fincke notes the team was given only eight minutes; individual sheets also describe an unreadable or unclear schedule. [PDR_reviews.pdf pp. 19, 21-22] [p. 1: Org Chart, Overview, Baseline design; p. 2: General notes]
priorities.suggested_action: Build and rehearse a concise deck that covers all rubric elements, retaining details in backup material.

vitabee.label: Imported pilot draft; not regenerated or independently revalidated
